Identifiability limits in AIMO-Interp Anonymous Author(s) Abstract On the frozen AIMO-Interp public validation board (14 Small and 21 Main items, inferred from the score grid), no score below perfect is separable from the independent fair-coin null after per-owner selection and across-owner Benjamini– Hochberg correction: 59 of 61 Small owners and 40 of 41 Main owners are not rejected, including an owner with a 12/14 Small result.
[11] We do not identify which owners were affected.
Our hash-pinned analysis adjusts each owner’s best visible score for its number of scored submissions under an independent-submission model.
A single pre-specified predictor needs at least 76 independent correctness items at true accuracy 0.65, or 169 at 0.6, to sustain power 0.8 at level 0.05 before selection correction.
We provide CPU reproduction rather than additional model runs.
Both reference baselines were scored once each through the organizers’ temporary evaluation queue during the Codabench outage [11]; these runs are not on the leaderboard.
